what: The verifier that the published 0.4.2 archive actually contains
why: The 0.2.1 DOI carried six checks and stayed silent about the rest. This baseline records, from the downloaded archive itself, what the 0.4.2 archive carries, so that a claim about S1-S19 can be checked against the file rather than remembered.
how_measured: curl --resolve zenodo.org:443:<IP> downloaded the archive through the poisoned-DNS host; the zip was unpacked and uibc_core/verify.py was hashed and regex-scanned for quoted S-ids. At the moment of measurement the file was byte-identical (same sha256, 69835 bytes) to the copy in main, so the archive is not a stale snapshot of the verifier.
limits_of_this_measurement: It measures CHECK IDS, not behaviour. A count of ids says nothing about how much each id actually inspects.
S0 is a fallback branch, not a nineteenth check of the same rank as the rest; it is listed so the count is not silently off by one.
The bundled 28-case corpus exercises 15 of the 20 ids. S9 and S19 are built inside the oracle tool's own code and are not shipped as packages in the corpus.
The archive matched main on the day it was published; main moves. The hash above is the fact, the equality is a dated observation.
